Rescue The Generation · Umeå ↔ Addis Ababa · Est. 2020

It Concerns Me.

ያገባኛል — Yagebanal. The word our founders chose. It means the hunger of a stranger is my business. We are a volunteer-run Ethiopian charity, founded by the diaspora in Sweden, working where the need is greatest — one school, one mother, one generation at a time.

A bridge, not a headquarters

Who we are

Founded in 2020 by Ethiopian doctors, engineers and teachers living in Scandinavia, RTG moves resources from those who left to those who stayed.

We are non-profit, non-political and autonomous. Our board members are emergency physicians, public-health directors and development practitioners with decades in the field — people who know that in a crisis, time is life.

We respond to emergencies, confront the roots of poverty and violence against women and children, and stand with children with special needs. And because trust is our only currency, we publish what we do, where, and what it cost.

The work, right now

Programs · 2025–26
01

Digital classrooms

Afar Region · with local schools

Fully equipped computers, pre-loaded with offline educational material — because a school beyond the reach of the internet shouldn't be beyond the reach of knowledge.

Offlinefirst design
02

Dignity, monthly

Debre Birhan University

Sanitary-pad support for female students who cannot afford it — so no one misses an exam for being poor.

Everymonth, term-round
03

School materials

Shewa Robit

Books, pens and supplies for students whose families and guardians cannot provide them.

30+students accepted
04

Youth sports development

Debre Birhan · with Tesfa Sports Center & local government

We supply the kit, Tesfa supplies the coaches. Two trainees have already advanced to the Addis Ababa Academy — and every year the annual festival brings athletics and football to the whole town.

85+youths in training
05

Health insurance

Addis Ababa

Digital health insurance covering a full year of medical costs for disabled and elderly residents who would otherwise go untreated.

50+people covered
06

Emergency relief

Gamo Zone · landslide response

Direct financial support delivered to families hit by the recent landslide — fast, documented, and in full.

500Kbirr delivered
07

Single mothers tailoring co-op

Completed · handed over

Training, machines and a workspace — then the keys. The women now run the workshop themselves. Read the story below.

100%independently run

Earlier chapters: IDP relief in Debre Berhan (2022–23), soft loans to 45 women in Shewa Robit, sewing training for 20 women with Muluwengel Church, 30 computers to Shewa-Robit High School with Camara Education, generator restoration for Ataye Hospital. Next: the Geferssa water-rehabilitation center and the Wag Himra livelihood project.

Field report

Single mothers tailoring project · Completed

The machines
are theirs now.

A group of single mothers. A hired trainer. Sewing machines and materials bought, a workspace facilitated by the local government. Months of training.

Then the part that matters: the handover. The machines were formally given to the women — and today they manufacture women's clothing and undergarments, run their own orders, and answer to no one but each other.

Our job was to leave. That's what rescue looks like.

  1. ፩Trainer hired, machines & materials purchased
  2. ፪Workspace facilitated by local government
  3. ፫Training completed · machines handed over
  4. ፬Production running — women's clothing & undergarments
